session_cue.text: The invisible Clurichen slipping on Phidipaldi's marbles

previous.text: Trout recruited Squints, a newly arrived halfling, as junior assistant in his Halfling Corps. Trout later put the rescued Brother Dirk under Squints.
The party caught Naggeneen, the invisible Clurichen stealing Quinn's booze, and handed him over to Quinn.
Dunk spotted a glowing magical mithril chain shirt in Warwick the smith's shop and told the party he had a plan to get it.
Dunk struck a deal with Ingrid the Alchemist for a sleeping potion. He got wine from the fauns and gave her a watered-down batch.
George the woodsman described the dragon's deadly powers and lair, and doubted the Reeve can pay the bounty.
The party set out for Sir Brandon's Barrow Mound after Father William pointed them to the sword buried there.
Squints pulled Brother Dirk from a sleeping giant's sack, and the party outran the waking giant across a field.

current.where_you_are: The party is in the field near the giant's cyclopean cottage in the woods north of Brandonsford. Squints and the freed Brother Dirk are with them.

Your goals.text: Acquire the mithril chain shirt from Warwick the smith's shop.
Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Fight Eric the Reeve in the dawn duel Sir Phidipaldi challenged him to.

Standing in your way.text: George says nothing pierces the dragon's black scales. Its poisonous bite kills, and it spits sulfur.
Farmer Gill won't lower his price for Shamus until his boys return, since he can't work without them or a mule.
Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell his mithril chain shirt.

What could help.text: The party holds a treasure map marking several unrecognized locations near Brandonsford.
If Dunk helps Ingrid get her sleeping potion to Warwick, he could get into Warwick's house to take the shirt.
If Dunk meets Ingrid tonight, he can collect her sleeping potion and use it to put Warwick to sleep.
Father William says that if the party goes to Sir Brandon's Barrow Mound, they can retrieve the sword buried with him.
George says the dragon's lair lies north at the foot of the mountains, with no climbing needed.
If the party claims Sir Brandon's sword, they gain what is said to be the only way to kill the dragon.
If the party checks a marked map location on its way north through the forest, they could find the map's treasure.
If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will fight the dragon alongside them.
Squints has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant, taking orders directly from Trout.
Dunk says that if the party gets Warwick's mithril chain shirt, it could help them against the dragon.
If the party hires Lady Hilda, they gain a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield.
Dunk says that if the party gets Warwick's mithril chain shirt, they will have magical armor.
If the party pays Drop Dead Ned 100 gold a week, he and his killer wasp will do anything that lets him kill people.

Still unanswered.text: Why are the once-hidden fairies coming out more often?
Where did this new dragon come from?
Why has nothing reached Brandonsford in months?

Promises and debts.text: Dunk must help Ingrid get into Warwick's house and give him her sleeping potion, in return for her brewing it.
Dr. Uriah must do penance at the Barrow Mound and give Father William 10 gold for its upkeep.
Trout must let Squints pick from the Halfling Corps' first treasure after the elite members. Until then, Squints pays his own way.
Sir Phidipaldi must bring his lance against the dragon, as he vowed to George.
Sir Phidipaldi must come back for Lady Hilda's services after the party talks to the Reeve.

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon that tore off George's arm is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.
George says the dragon can't fly yet but soon will, and then they are doomed.
A slow giant in the cyclopean cottage captures people to eat, and Brother Dirk says he meant to stew him. The giant is now awake and chased the party.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: Dr. Uriah carries the map and plans to copy it, the party means to check a marked location on the way north, and Father William added marks to it. The treasure is still unfound.

threads.name: The Clurichen of the riverbanks
threads.note: The question of what the Clurichen does is answered: Naggeneen drinks Quinn's booze (beat_18). He is now captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar (beat_19, beat_37), and his offer of a pot of gold or a secret still stands, so the situation remains open in a new shape.

threads.name: The dragon and the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: George revealed where the lair is (beat_58), and the danger has escalated because the dragon will soon fly. The party learned the dragon can only be killed with Brandon's sword (beat_51), and George doubts the Reeve has the bounty (beat_60). The dragon is still alive.

threads.name: Hiring Lady Hilda
threads.note: Hilda was only seen in passing. Sir Phidipaldi's promise to return for her services is unreleased.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer
threads.note: Ned was only seen in passing, and his offer remains undecided.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipments
threads.note: Shipments still had not come in, and the cause is still unknown.

threads.name: Sir Phidipaldi's quarrel with Eric the Reeve
threads.note: Phidipaldi still scorns Eric as a man of no honor. Nothing shows the duel happened or was declined.

threads.name: Shamus the mule
threads.note: Gill is willing to go lower than his price and would drop it once his boys return, but no deal for the mule is made yet.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Dunk confirmed the shirt is magical, scouted Warwick's house and has a plan to get it, but he does not have it yet.

threads.name: Quinn's revenge on Bentley
threads.note: The thief turned out to be Naggeneen, not Bentley (beat_18), and Quinn paid the party for catching him (beat_19). Nothing remains owed or unknown.

threads.name: Squints and Trout's Halfling Corps
threads.note: Trout recruited Squints on stated terms, including picks after the first treasure, and that arrangement is ongoing. Trout's secret intent not to rescue him also belongs to this relationship.

threads.name: Ingrid's sleeping potion for Warwick
threads.note: Dunk's bargain with Ingrid is one deal: he supplies the faun wine and helps her dose Warwick, she makes the potion, and he holds her secret. Dunk stated it serves his plan to get Warwick's armor (beat_33, beat_44). The potion is not yet made, and they are to meet tonight.

threads.name: Sir Brandon's magic sword at the Barrow Mound
threads.note: Father William says the dragon can't be killed without the sword buried with Brandon (beat_51), so this serves the dragon hunt. The party is heading to the Barrow, and Brother Dirk's willingness to continue is unsettled (beat_86).

threads.name: Dr. Uriah's penance and donation at the Barrow Mound
threads.note: Uriah promised Father William penance at the Barrow Mound and a 10 gold donation for its upkeep. That promise is still owed.

threads.name: Why the hidden fairies are coming out
threads.note: Ingrid reports that fairies which used to stay hidden are encroaching more often. This is an unexplained change that stands apart from the dragon.

threads.name: The giant in the cyclopean cottage
threads.note: A man-eating giant on the road north woke as the party rescued Dirk, then chased them until he tired. Escaping him does not end the danger.

facts.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations they do not recognize, near Brandonsford.

classification.support_basis: The map's marks are the party's only guide to where the treasure might be.

facts.text: Where is the treasure the map marks?

classification.grounding_justification: The map marks several unrecognized locations, so which holds the treasure is clearly unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it is mainly locating a place, a single discovery.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Finding the treasure's location is useful but mainly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Several marked locations can be visited and checked, supporting following leads.

facts.text: The party plans to check one of the map's marked locations on its way north through the forest.

classification.support_basis: Visiting a marked location could reveal whether the treasure lies there.
classification.action_basis: The party agreed to check a marked location while travelling north, which they are already doing.

facts.text: Where did the party's treasure map come from?

classification.grounding_justification: Dr. Uriah tried and could recall nothing of the map's history, raising the gap only loosely.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Its origin is a single fact unless it turns out to connect to more.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting background with no established mystery.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little established to pursue beyond asking around.

facts.text: Reginald the Frog says a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: no longer relevant: the Clurichen, Naggeneen, was caught and now hangs in a bag behind Quinn's bar

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The creature was only said to be up to no good, with no particular harm named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Any harm suggested was mischief at most.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Nightly visits were reported, but no escalating harm.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could avoid or catch it, as it did.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town each night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen sneaks into the Golden Egg's basement to drink Quinn's booze

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's warning made its nightly activity conspicuous.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer was a hidden circumstance, the booze theft.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supported a stakeout and tracking.

facts.text: Naggeneen, held in a bag behind Quinn's bar at the Golden Egg, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go.

classification.support_basis: No established want or debt of the party is served by the gold or secret.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen offered the trade, but he is now Quinn's captive and freeing him would need access or Quinn's consent that play has not established.

facts.resource_subject: Naggeneen held captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with the captive Naggeneen?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn pointedly said he knew what he would do with him without saying what, and kept him hanging behind the bar.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting, mainly about a minor character's fate.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Asking Quinn would likely settle it.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon troubling Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
George, a woodsman living a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox who may come to the tavern tonight, met the dragon and lost an arm to it; the party could question him about the dragon.
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi questioned George about the dragon

classification.support_basis: George's firsthand experience could tell the party where the dragon is and how it fights.
classification.action_basis: George was a known survivor living nearby who could be visited.

facts.text: Lady Hilda would join the party against the dragon for pay (see her offer's thread).

classification.support_basis: An extra fighter would add strength against the dragon, though its scales resist ordinary weapons.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda offered to join for pay.

facts.text: Where is the black dragon to be found?
facts.ended_how: answered: George says the lair is up north at the foot of the mountains (beat_58)

classification.grounding_justification: The bounty required finding the dragon and its location was not known.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A location; one discovery settles it.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be answered by questioning a survivor.

facts.text: Where has this new dragon come from, centuries after Sir Brandon killed the first?

classification.grounding_justification: A dragon has appeared long after the legendary one was slain, and George says no one knows what is true of the old tale.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause of the dragon's return.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Would explain the central event of the adventure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Fairytales known to Farmer Gill and the Barrow offer leads.

facts.text: The black dragon, which tore off George the woodsman's arm, is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Maiming or killing of people near Brandonsford is specific.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Its bite kills and it killed George's friends.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's direct testimony and lost arm.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: It has already attacked, but no new attacks on town are reported.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing it with Brandon's sword is a plausible but uncertain path.

facts.text: Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting the dragon now and could kill it before the party, taking the Reeve's bounty.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Losing the bounty is a specific outcome.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Loss of the reward is meaningful but not physical harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Known they hunt it, but the dragon seems near unkillable without the sword.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: They are hunting, but success is unlikely given failed weapons.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could race to kill it first.

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is up north at the foot of the mountains, with no climbing needed.

classification.support_basis: Tells the party where to find the dragon, which they did not know.

facts.text: Nothing pierces the dragon's black scales: George says his friends' arrows and swords all failed, and Father William says it can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Sir Brandon. Its jaws drip poison whose bite kills, and it spits sulfur.

classification.scope_basis: The dragon's invulnerability is an inherent property that will apply whenever the party confronts it.

facts.text: The magic sword buried with Sir Brandon at the Barrow Mound is said to be the only way to kill the dragon (see its thread).

classification.support_basis: Father William says the dragon cannot be killed without it, though George says no one knows what is true or where the sword is.
classification.action_basis: The party is already walking to the Barrow Mound to get the sword.

facts.resource_subject: The magic sword buried with Sir Brandon, needed to kill the dragon

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt could help against the dragon (see its thread).

classification.support_basis: Magical armor could protect against the dragon's poison bite and sulfur, though how well is unestablished.
classification.action_basis: Dunk has a plan underway to get the armor from Warwick.

facts.resource_subject: Warwick's magical mithril chain shirt and its potential use against the dragon

facts.text: George says the dragon can't fly yet but soon will, and then they are doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: A flying dragon dooming the region is suggested, but the exact harm is vague.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Doom for the town and its people.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Testimony of a survivor who saw the dragon.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George says flight is coming soon, an advancing process, though no timeline.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon before it flies is identifiable but depends on getting the sword.

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.grounding_justification: George explicitly doubts the Reeve has the money.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A bounded fact about the Reeve's funds.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Would matter practically and might reveal the Reeve as dishonest.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by questioning townsfolk or the Reeve.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon, which George allows may be one of the few weapons not yet tried.

classification.stake_basis: George wants the dragon killed as repayment but only allowed the lance might be untried; no reliance on the lance itself is established.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield, offers to join the party against the dragon for pay.

classification.support_basis: An extra seasoned fighter adds strength against the dragon, though George says arrows and swords have all failed against its scales.
classification.action_basis: Hilda herself offered to join against the dragon for pay; the party can hire her on her terms.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk to the Reeve and then come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: Hilda offered her services for pay, so she has a modest interest in the party returning to hire her; no reliance beyond that is established.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp in a jar, offers himself and the wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill people; Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.support_basis: Ned and his killer wasp would add a hired fighter toward the dragon hunt, though nothing shows the wasp could harm a dragon whose scales nothing pierces.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services at 100 gold a week, and he is still at the Clumsy Fox.

facts.text: Why has nothing come into Brandonsford in months, including Bentley's restock shipment that was due a week ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Months without any shipments into town, confirmed again this Session as still ongoing, is a conspicuous anomaly.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause behind a town-wide supply failure.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning what is cutting off the town would explain events and may connect to the wider dangers.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It plausibly supports following trade routes and questioning merchants such as Bentley.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in the duel he challenged him to at dawn.
Will Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi, accept his challenge to a duel at dawn?

classification.grounding_justification: An earlier session established the challenge and Eric's offense; this session shows Phidipaldi still scorns Eric but nothing about the duel's outcome.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple yes-or-no about Eric's response.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting personal drama, mostly routine.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by asking Eric or showing up at dawn.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus; Gill asked 100 gold but says he is willing to go lower.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill said the big work needed is killing the dragon; he did not say outright he would give the mule for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon might earn the mule, but Gill never agreed to that exchange, so its value is doubtful.
classification.action_basis: Gill only named the dragon as the big work needed; he did not offer the mule in exchange, so a deal would be invented.

facts.text: Farmer Gill can get no work done without his boys or a mule, so he won't drop his price for Shamus until his boys come back.

classification.scope_basis: Gill tied the lower price to his boys' return, a condition that lasts until they come home.

facts.text: Acquire the mithril chain shirt Warwick the smith displays in his shop.
Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays.

classification.scope_basis: Warwick's refusal to sell is a standing policy reported by Gill, not a single encounter, and the shirt is still on display.

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt is magical armor that could help against the dragon, once the party has it.

classification.support_basis: Magical armor could offer protection against the dragon's poisonous bite and attacks, though what its magic actually does is unknown.
classification.action_basis: The shirt is clearly magical armor and the dragon is an established danger the party means to fight; wearing armor against it is a straightforward match, but the shirt must first be acquired.

facts.resource_subject: Warwick's magical mithril chain shirt and its potential use against the dragon

facts.text: Dunk's plan to help Ingrid get her sleeping potion to Warwick could let him into Warwick's house to take the shirt.

classification.support_basis: With Warwick drugged asleep and Dunk inside, he could take the shirt Warwick refuses to sell.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion and Dunk arranged to meet her to deliver it; Dunk told the party this is his plan for the armor.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's mithril chain shirt hold?

classification.grounding_justification: The shirt glows and is clearly magical, but its powers are simply not described.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying an item's property is a simple fact.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Likely settled by examining or wearing the shirt.

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
facts.ended_how: achieved: the thief turned out to be Naggeneen, not Bentley; the party caught him and Quinn paid Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each

facts.text: Quinn's plan: he brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to stage a fake shipment.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught in the basement without the plan and Quinn has paid

classification.support_basis: The staged shipment was meant to lure the stock thief so Quinn could catch him.
classification.action_basis: Quinn himself proposed the plan and would supply the bottles.

facts.text: What empties or knocks over Quinn's stock every night? Quinn blames Bentley.
facts.ended_how: answered: the Clurichen Naggeneen was drinking Quinn's booze, not Bentley

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn's stock was being emptied nightly by an unseen culprit, explicitly framed as a mystery.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer revealed a hidden culprit behind repeated thefts.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Revealing an invisible fairy rather than Bentley reframed Quinn's grudge.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supported a stakeout and tracking footprints from the river.

facts.text: Under Trout's recruitment terms, once the Halfling Corps finds its first treasure Squints gets to pick from it after the elite members; until then Squints funds himself and his gear and takes orders from Trout.

classification.stake_basis: Squints came to Brandonsford seeking his big break and agreed to fund himself and fight monsters on the promise of treasure picks.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling more experienced at fighting than Trout and armed with a sling and dagger, has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant and takes orders directly from Trout.

classification.support_basis: An extra experienced fighter who agreed to fight monsters immediately adds strength to the party's dragon hunt, though not against the dragon's unpierceable scales specifically.

facts.text: Trout, with Phidipaldi's agreement, secretly intends not to rescue Squints if he is caught while sent into danger, despite promising him intervention.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The harm is Squints being left to his fate when caught on a dangerous task.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Squints could be captured or killed, serious harm to one person.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Trout stated the intent aloud and Phidipaldi agreed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Trout already sent Squints into the giant's cottage once; no further dangerous task is set.
classification.preventability_justification: The party itself can choose to rescue Squints or not send him into danger.

facts.text: Dunk owes Ingrid help getting into Warwick's house and giving Warwick her sleeping potion, so she can watch him sleep without fear of waking him, in exchange for her making the potion.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid fears Warwick waking while she watches him, and agreed to make the potion on the strength of Dunk helping her dose him.

facts.text: Ingrid is making a sleeping potion from the faun wine Dunk gave her; Dunk can collect it when they meet tonight and use it to put Warwick to sleep.

classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick would let Dunk take the mithril chain shirt unopposed, though Dunk diluted the faun wine to about 20%, so its strength is in doubt.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion and set the meeting; the faun wine puts creatures to sleep.

facts.text: Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom above his shop whose window is left cracked open; Ingrid climbs up to it every night.

classification.support_basis: The open window is a way into Warwick's home, where the mithril chain shirt is kept, and a way to reach him to give the potion.
classification.action_basis: The window is observed cracked open and Ingrid climbs to it nightly, so climbing in is a supported physical option.

facts.text: Dunk knows Ingrid secretly watches Warwick sleep every night, which she dreads him learning, and he has hinted he might not keep it secret.

classification.support_basis: The secret gives Dunk leverage to keep Ingrid cooperating on the potion and the entry into Warwick's house.

facts.text: The fauns of the Faun Grove trade their faun wine for sentimental items such as a love letter or a pixie's treasure.

classification.support_basis: More faun wine could make a stronger or replacement sleeping potion if the diluted batch falls short.
classification.action_basis: Dunk already traded a rabbit's foot for a flask, showing the fauns accept such trades.

facts.text: Will a potion made from Dunk's heavily diluted faun wine still put Warwick to sleep?

classification.grounding_justification: Dunk deliberately cut the key ingredient to about 20% with tavern wine, clearly raising doubt about potency.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple property of the potion, settled by testing it.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond a test or asking Ingrid.

facts.text: Does Ingrid really make her potions herself, as she claims, or can't she, as Father William says?

classification.grounding_justification: Father William and Ingrid directly contradict each other.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: It could reveal a hidden arrangement with the witch Vivian, but is mostly a yes-or-no fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting given the coven claim, mainly bearing on whether the potion gets made.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by watching her work or asking Vivian.

facts.text: Father William says the dragon can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Sir Brandon in his Barrow Mound; the party could go to the Barrow and retrieve it.

classification.support_basis: Father William says the sword is required to kill a dragon whose scales nothing has pierced, but George says no one knows what is true about the sword or where it is.
classification.action_basis: The party knows the Barrow's location from Father William's map marking and has already set out to walk there.

facts.resource_subject: The magic sword buried with Sir Brandon, needed to kill the dragon

facts.text: Father William marked the Barrow Mound's location on Dr. Uriah's map; he says it is about a day's walk away, while the party also heard it is roughly a three-mile walk through the forest.

classification.support_basis: The marked map lets the party find the Barrow where the sword is said to lie, though the distance estimates conflict.

facts.resource_subject: Where the Barrow Mound is and how far away it is

facts.text: Will Brother Dirk continue to the Barrow with the party, or go home?

classification.grounding_justification: Dirk said he should just go home while Phidipaldi and Uriah pushed back, leaving his choice explicitly unsettled.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: It is a simple decision by one person, not a hidden truth.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly practical; mildly interesting given Father William's reliance on Dirk.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by talking with Dirk directly.

facts.text: Is Sir Brandon's magic sword really buried in his Barrow Mound?

classification.grounding_justification: Father William says the sword is buried with Brandon, but George says no one knows what is true or where the sword is, a clear contradiction.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: One visit to the Barrow would largely settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Useful for the dragon hunt and touches the Brandon legend, but mainly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could involve exploring the Barrow and asking Farmer Gill about the fairytales.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at the Barrow Mound and a 10 gold donation for the Mound's upkeep.

classification.stake_basis: Father William, the town priest, asked for the penance and the donation toward the Barrow Mound's upkeep, and he marked the Mound on Uriah's map. That shows a modest interest in the Mound's care and in Uriah's penance. Nothing beyond this is shown to depend on it.

facts.text: Why are fairies that used to stay hidden now encroaching and coming out more often, as Ingrid reports?

classification.grounding_justification: Ingrid explicitly reports a recent change in fairy behaviour, set apart from the dragon, with no explanation given.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause behind a change in the wood folk's behaviour.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning the cause could explain events in the forest and change the party's understanding of local fey activity.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Ingrid and her forest-dwelling witch friend Vivian, who sees the fairies, are sources that could be questioned and followed up.

facts.text: A slow-moving giant living in an oversized cottage of cyclopean rocks in the woods north of Brandonsford captures people to eat; Brother Dirk says the giant meant to cook him in a stew. The giant is now awake and chased the party until he tired.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The specific harm is being captured and eaten, as Dirk nearly was.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The party saw Dirk bound in a sack beside the giant's cooking pot, and Dirk testifies he was to be stewed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The giant has already captured Dirk and chased the party, but nothing shows he will pursue them or strike again beyond his cottage.
classification.preventability_justification: The giant is slow and easily outrun, and the party knows where his cottage is and can avoid it.
